headline: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as Israel pulls back
pages: Residents of southern Lebanon are returning to damaged homes as the Israeli army pulls back from the area. NPR visited Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, where one family came home in July under a US-brokered plan for Israeli forces to withdraw and the Lebanese army to take over. They found their house had been occupied by Israeli soldiers and then set on fire. Their youngest son, a volunteer ambulance driver, was killed with four other medics in a drone strike on March 28. The Israeli military said without proof that militants pose as paramedics. Lebanon's Health Ministry says Israel has killed more than 135 first responders in two years.
Israel's defense minister has acknowledged destroying more than 20,000 homes in a self-declared security zone. The plan aims to keep Hezbollah out of the area. Source: NPR.
